hypothesis: Event-time order-flow features (OFI, trade imbalance, queue pressure, microprice displacement) combined with separate return-magnitude and fill-probability models, evaluated through walk-forward validation with realistic maker/taker execution costs, will achieve positive net executable EV on BTCUSDT 10s horizon. V15 proved GBR can predict return magnitude in-sample (R2=0.82) but failed forward because (a) model overfit, (b) fixed 75% fill probability was unrealistic, (c) no walk-forward validation. V16 addresses all three.
feature_construction: event-time (not fixed bars) — features computed at each order-book event
queue_pressure_definition: Queue pressure = (depth_added_at_touch - depth_removed_at_touch) / (depth_added_at_touch + depth_removed_at_touch + eps) over the lookback window. This is a proxy for queue position: high queue pressure means more orders are being added than removed at the touch, suggesting the queue is growing and new orders are behind existing ones. Limitations: does not account for order sizes, hidden liquidity, or cross-exchange queue dynamics.
target_definition: 10s forward mid-price return in bps (regression target). Separate binary target for fill probability (was the order filled within 10s at the predicted price or better?).

models.baseline: naive mean return + naive fill rate

stopping_rule: If V16 fails economic gate, conclude BTCUSDT short-horizon order-flow strategy is not economically viable under tested conditions. Do NOT create V17.
data_rules: Forward capture must start AFTER calibration ends
Model frozen before any forward data seen
